archeomapsSnapshot.name: Forbidden City
archeomapsSnapshot.description: The imperial palace of China, built 1406-1420 under the Ming Yongle Emperor when he moved the capital from Nanjing to Beijing. It served as home and seat of power for 24 emperors across the Ming and Qing dynasties until the last emperor, Puyi, was forced out in 1924. The complex holds nearly 1,000 surviving buildings and roughly 8,700 rooms behind a moat and 30-foot walls. Converted into the Palace Museum in 1925, it remains one of the largest and best-preserved collections of ancient wooden architecture in the world and was named a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.
